result: The proposed estimator achieves the same asymptotic distribution as the MLE and attains the smallest possible asymptotic maximum risk; new fluctuation results for the Hamiltonian and partition function are also obtained.
conclusion: This work provides the first sharp asymptotic optimality results for network-dependent data, with implications for inference in Ising models on random graphs.

title: Information-Theoretic Bounds For Sparse Covariance Estimation In The Vertical-Split Distributed Model
authors: Guangyue Han Jing Yee Tan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the minimax estimation error for distributed covariance matrix estimation in the vertical-split (feature-split) setting, where two agents each observe different coordinates of [MATH] i.i.d. sub-Gaussian samples and communicate a limited number of bits to a central server. While Rahmani et al. [2025] established nearly tight bounds for dense (unstructured) cross-covariance matrices, we investigate whether imposing elementwise [MATH]-sparsity on the cross-covariance [MATH] can reduce the required communication and sample complexity. In contrast to the horizontal-split setting, where Braverman et al. [2016] showed that sparsity does not reduce communication cost for mean estimation, we prove that sparsity does help for cross-covariance estimation in the vertical split. Specifically, we establish minimax lower bounds showing that the communication budget per agent scales as [MATH] and the sample complexity for cross-covariance estimation as [MATH], where [MATH]. For the [MATH]-sparse case, this yields an exponential improvement from [MATH] to [MATH] compared to the dense rate. Our lower bounds are established via Fano's method with an explicit sparse packing using a Varshamov--Gilbert-type argument for signed partial permutation matrices combined with the Conditional Strong Data Processing Inequality of Rahmani et al. [2025]. We show the bounds are tight with a matching achievable scheme, based on covering-net quantization and entry-wise hard thresholding, that attains the [MATH]-sparse lower bound up to polylogarithmic factors.
tldr: This paper studies minimax bounds for sparse covariance estimation in a distributed vertical-split model, showing that sparsity reduces communication and sample complexity.
motivation: To understand whether sparsity can reduce communication and sample complexity in distributed covariance estimation, which is a fundamental problem in statistical learning.
method: The authors use Fano's method with a sparse packing argument based on signed partial permutation matrices and the Conditional Strong Data Processing Inequality to derive lower bounds, and propose a matching achievable scheme using covering-net quantization and hard thresholding.
result: They prove that for elementwise s-sparse cross-covariance matrices, the communication budget per agent scales as s log(p) and sample complexity as s^2 log(p), an exponential improvement over the dense case.
conclusion: Sparsity helps reduce communication and sample complexity in the vertical-split distributed model, and the bounds are tight up to polylog factors.

title: On A Small Version Of The Reflection Equation Algebra
authors: Stephen T. Moore
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an alternative presentation of the small version of the reflection equation algebra associated to [MATH] at both odd and even roots of unity, and use our presentation to classify its irreducible representations. We then describe a family of algebras generalizing the small reflection equation algebra, and consider their application to the study of module categories over [MATH] fusion categories.
tldr: This paper studies the small reflection equation algebra and its representations at roots of unity, with applications to fusion categories.
motivation: The reflection equation algebra arises in quantum groups and integrable systems; the small version is less studied. The authors aim to classify its irreducible representations and generalize the algebra.
method: The authors provide an alternative presentation of the small reflection equation algebra and use it to classify irreducible representations. They then define a family of generalized algebras.
result: A classification of irreducible representations is obtained, and a family of algebras generalizing the small reflection equation algebra is described.
conclusion: The work contributes to the representation theory of quantum groups at roots of unity and may have implications for fusion categories.

title: No-Harm Physics-Informed Inverse Learning With Residual-Calibrated Uncertainty
authors: Ronald Katende
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed learning is increasingly used for partial differential equation (PDE)-governed inverse problems, but its reliability remains difficult to certify. This paper develops a no-harm certification-and-selection framework for physics-informed inverse learning. A learned reconstruction is accepted only when its residual-calibrated radius is no worse than the baseline radius, namely when $[MATH]$otherwise, the method returns the baseline. The certificate combines data, physics, boundary or initial-condition, and optimization residuals. Under a conditional stability estimate, these residuals yield an a posteriori reconstruction-error bound and a deterministic uncertainty radius. A high-probability certificate is also derived for physics residuals estimated from independent random collocation points. Numerical tests on Poisson source recovery, inverse heat reconstruction, limited-angle tomography, elliptic coefficient identification, and stochastic residual validation show that the selector accepts certified improvements, rejects shifted, hallucinated, or unfinished candidates, and becomes conservative in strongly ill-posed regimes. The framework is therefore a certification-and-selection layer, not another reconstruction architecture.
tldr: A no-harm certification-and-selection framework for physics-informed inverse learning that accepts reconstructions only when their residual-calibrated uncertainty is no worse than a baseline.
motivation: Physics-informed learning for PDE-governed inverse problems lacks reliability certification, making it difficult to trust learned reconstructions.
method: The framework combines data, physics, boundary, and optimization residuals into an a posteriori error bound and deterministic uncertainty radius, and uses a conditional stability estimate to certify reconstructions.
result: Numerical tests on Poisson source recovery, inverse heat reconstruction, limited-angle tomography, and elliptic coefficient identification show the selector accepts certified improvements and rejects shifted or hallucinated candidates.
conclusion: The framework provides a certification-and-selection layer that can be added to any reconstruction method, improving reliability without requiring a new architecture.

title: The Synthesis-Sequencing Channel For DNA-based Data Storage
authors: Keshav Goyal, Samuel Pearson, Jo\~ao Ribeiro, Serge Kas Hanna
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study the synthesis-sequencing channel, a two-stage model for DNA-based data storage that jointly captures synthesis and sequencing effects. The synthesis-sequencing channel provides a more nuanced and realistic model of the DNA storage process compared to prior work, as it distinguishes between physical coverage after synthesis and sequencing coverage after readout, relaxes the assumption of independent errors across reads, and naturally induces coverage bias through the composition of synthesis and sequencing stages. We establish the information-theoretic capacity of this channel by deriving matching converse and achievability bounds for the case where synthesis and sequencing errors are modeled by binary symmetric channels with possibly different error probabilities, under mild assumptions on the channel parameters. Our results reveal multiple trade-offs between physical coverage, synthesis errors, sequencing coverage, and sequencing errors that influence the maximum achievable rate for reliable data storage.
tldr: This paper introduces a synthesis-sequencing channel model for DNA-based data storage and derives its information-theoretic capacity.
motivation: DNA storage is a promising archival medium, but realistic channel models are needed to understand fundamental limits.
method: The authors model the storage process as a two-stage channel with binary symmetric errors and derive matching converse and achievability bounds.
result: The capacity is characterized, revealing trade-offs between physical coverage, synthesis errors, sequencing coverage, and sequencing errors.
conclusion: The results provide theoretical guidance for designing reliable DNA storage systems.

title: Fast Bounded-Independence Functions And Their Duals
authors: Martijn Brehm, Yuval Ishai, Nicolas Resch
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We continue the study of {\em fast} functions, computable by linear-size circuits, that share useful properties of random functions. Motivated by cryptographic applications, we generalize and improve on previous results in this area, obtaining the following results: - For any constant [MATH], we construct a fast [MATH]-wise independent hash function with algebraic degree [MATH] (over [MATH]), simultaneously optimizing both asymptotic circuit size and degree. - We simplify and improve a recent construction (ITCS 2026) of a family of fast codes with fast duals, both meeting the Gilbert-Varshamov bound. Unlike the previous construction, our construction has negligible failure probability, can accommodate general fields and rates, supports a systematic encoding, and admits fast universal encoders. - We strengthen the above to support stronger random-like properties, such as optimal combinatorial list-decoding. This is achieved by constructing, for any constant [MATH], a family of fast linear functions that map any [MATH] linearly independent inputs to uniform and statistically independent outputs. Prior to our work, this was only known for [MATH]. We demonstrate the usefulness of the above results to cryptography. This includes the first nontrivial protocols for perfectly secure multiparty computation whose circuit complexity scales linearly with the number of parties, as well as protocols for computing encrypted matrix-vector products with optimal asymptotic circuit complexity.
tldr: Constructs fast bounded-independence hash functions and codes with fast duals, with applications to cryptography and secure multiparty computation.
motivation: To design functions computable by linear-size circuits that mimic random functions, improving efficiency in cryptographic protocols.
method: Generalizes and simplifies previous constructions using algebraic degree optimization and linear functions over finite fields.
result: Achieves optimal asymptotic circuit size and degree for hash functions, codes meeting the Gilbert-Varshamov bound with negligible failure probability, and supports stronger random-like properties.
conclusion: These constructions enable the first nontrivial perfectly secure MPC protocols with linear circuit complexity and optimal encrypted matrix-vector products.

title: Sort, Partition, Randomize: Optimal Binary Hypothesis Testing Under Local Differential Privacy
authors: Elena Ghazi, Jawad Nasser, Flavio Calmon, Ibrahim Issa
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study optimal design of [MATH]-locally differentially private mechanisms for binary hypothesis testing. Each observation is drawn from one of two known distributions [MATH] on a finite alphabet of size [MATH], privatized by a mechanism [MATH], and then used to infer which distribution generated the data. We measure testing utility using an [MATH]-divergence, including total variation, KL, and hockey-stick divergences, between the two induced output distributions. Previous work established structural properties of optimal mechanisms, but only yielded exponential-time algorithms. We prove a sharp structure: for every [MATH] and every [MATH]-divergence objective, after sorting the alphabet by likelihood ratio, there exists an optimal mechanism that partitions the sorted alphabet into contiguous blocks and applies randomized response to the block label. We call this class Sort-Partition-Randomize (SPR). This characterization yields an exact dynamic program that computes an optimal mechanism in [MATH] time, and more generally in [MATH] time with an [MATH]-output budget. Our results make it possible to efficiently compute and characterize the exact optimum across the full privacy range, beyond asymptotic privacy regimes.
tldr: This paper studies optimal locally differentially private mechanisms for binary hypothesis testing using f-divergences, proving a structural characterization that enables efficient computation.
motivation: Designing optimal privacy-preserving mechanisms for hypothesis testing is important but previous algorithms were exponential-time; a more efficient characterization is needed.
method: The authors prove that for any f-divergence, an optimal mechanism sorts the alphabet by likelihood ratio, partitions it into contiguous blocks, and applies randomized response to the block label, leading to a dynamic programming algorithm.
result: The Sort-Partition-Randomize (SPR) class characterizes optimal mechanisms, and an exact dynamic program computes the optimum in O(k^3) time, or O(k^2) with an output budget.
conclusion: The work provides a complete, efficient solution to optimal binary hypothesis testing under local differential privacy across the full privacy range.

title: Passive All-optical Synchronization For Polarization-maintaining Ultrafast Fiber Lasers
authors: Kun Huang, Jing Zeng, Jiwei Gan, Qiang Hao, Ming Yan, Heping Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We have proposed and implemented for the first time to our best knowledge a passive and all-optical pulse synchronization for polarization-maintaining ultrafast fiber lasers. Specifically, the synchronization system was comprised of two independent Yb-doped and Er-doped mode-locked fiber lasers in a master-slave configuration. Master pulses were injected into the slave laser cavity consisting of a nonlinear amplifying loop mirror, which provided an effective fast intensity modulator due to the periodic introduction of nonreciprocal phase difference. As a result, robust and tight timing synchronization was achieved with a cavity mismatch tolerance of 800 [MATH]m and a relative timing jitter of 26 fs within 1-MHz bandwidth. In combination with all-polarization-maintaining structure of fiber lasers, long-term stable operation was demonstrated over 12 hours without the need of temperature stabilization and vibration isolation. The implemented synchronous laser system could find immediate applications such as pump-probe microscopy, two-color spectroscopy and nonlinear frequency mixing.
tldr: This paper demonstrates passive all-optical synchronization of two polarization-maintaining ultrafast fiber lasers using a master-slave configuration with a nonlinear amplifying loop mirror.
motivation: To achieve robust, low-jitter synchronization of ultrafast lasers without active electronics, enabling applications like pump-probe microscopy and two-color spectroscopy.
method: Two independent Yb-doped and Er-doped mode-locked fiber lasers are synchronized by injecting master pulses into the slave laser cavity, which contains a nonlinear amplifying loop mirror that acts as a fast intensity modulator via nonreciprocal phase difference.
result: The system achieves a cavity mismatch tolerance of 800 μm and a relative timing jitter of 26 fs within 1-MHz bandwidth, with stable operation over 12 hours without temperature stabilization or vibration isolation.
conclusion: The passive all-optical synchronization method is effective and robust, suitable for practical applications requiring stable dual-color ultrafast laser sources.

title: Ultralow Shot Noise Limited Giant Passive Resonant Gyroscope For Earth Rotation Measurement
authors: Yuhong Zhong, Yangsheng Cai, Zhanhao Liu, Lei Zheng, Yunhe Wang, Xiaojun Huang, Zhiyuan Wang, Kui Liu, Liangcheng Tu, Jun Luo, Zehuang Lu, Jie Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical gyroscopes directly measure the Earth's rotation and are promising instruments for real-time geophysical observations and Earth orientation parameter (EOP) determination requiring both high precision and high temporal resolution. Large-scale ring laser gyroscopes (RLGs) currently reach rotational resolutions around [MATH], but their quantum noise limits make it challenging to meet the requirements of future high-temporal-resolution EOP measurements. Passive resonant gyroscopes (PRGs), on the other hand, offer a potentially lower photon shot noise limit and more flexible power scaling, even if their demonstrated rotational resolutions are still about two orders of magnitude below those of leading RLGs. Here we demonstrate a [MATH] giant passive resonant gyroscope HUST-2, and develop with an extremely low shot noise level. We experimentally obtain a shot noise limited of [MATH] at [MATH] incident optical power, following the characteristic [MATH] scaling. Through systematic suppression of dominant technical noise sources, HUST-2 further achieves a measured rotational resolution of [MATH], bringing PRGs into the performance regime of leading large-scale RLGs for the first time. The gap between the present demonstrated rotational resolution and the shot noise limit indicates nearly two orders of magnitude further improvement potential. Reaching this limit would enable high-precision length-of-day (LOD) measurements with [MATH]-[MATH] temporal resolution and lays the foundation for future large-scale gyroscope networks dedicated to real-time EOP determination.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a giant passive resonant gyroscope for Earth rotation measurement, achieving ultralow shot noise and high rotational resolution.
motivation: To improve the precision and temporal resolution of Earth rotation measurements for geophysical observations and Earth orientation parameter determination.
method: A 3-meter giant passive resonant gyroscope (HUST-2) is built, and technical noise sources are systematically suppressed to approach the shot noise limit.
result: The gyroscope achieves a rotational resolution of 1.2×10⁻⁹ rad/s, matching leading ring laser gyroscopes, with a shot noise limit of 4.5×10⁻¹¹ rad/s at 1 W optical power.
conclusion: Passive resonant gyroscopes can rival ring laser gyroscopes in performance and offer further improvement potential for high-temporal-resolution Earth rotation measurements.

title: Flash: Ultrafast Beam Quality Characterization Via Spatial-to-temporal Mapping
authors: J. Qiu, Y. Xiong, X. Hua, H. Wu, M. Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate and real-time monitoring of spatial beam quality has emerged as the absolute prerequisite for intelligent optical field regulation and advanced laser applications. However, modern high-power and multimode optical systems exhibit highly complex, nonlinear, and transient behaviors. In these systems, the spatial beam profile undergoes dramatic reorganizations within extremely short timeframes. Phenomena such as spatio-temporal mode-locking, transient beam self-cleaning, and plasma-induced aberrations demand nanosecond-level dynamic characterization. Yet, capturing these ultrafast dynamics is fundamentally bottlenecked by the kilohertz frame rates of conventional two-dimensional image sensors. To break this dimensional and temporal barrier, we propose an ultrafast non-imaging beam quality monitoring technique, termed Fiber-based Laser Assessment via Spatial-to-temporal High-speed-mapping (FLASH). By utilizing a multimode fiber to encode spatial beam variations into high-dimensional speckle fingerprints and a multicore fiber delay line array to serialize these features, we transform two-dimensional spatial information into high-speed one-dimensional temporal pulse sequences. Empowered by a deep learning model to decipher the serialized signals, the FLASH system achieves an unprecedented 100 MHz measurement rate with a minimal mean relative error of 0.32%. Realizing a five-order-of-magnitude speed improvement over standard camera-based methods, this spatial-to-temporal mapping paradigm provides a transformative spatial oscilloscope. It unlocks new possibilities for real-time intelligent adaptive control and the exploration of complex multimode nonlinear physics.
tldr: A technique using multimode fiber and deep learning to characterize laser beam quality at 100 MHz, far exceeding camera-based methods.
motivation: High-power multimode lasers exhibit ultrafast spatial beam dynamics that conventional cameras cannot capture due to kilohertz frame rates.
method: Spatial beam variations are encoded into speckle patterns via a multimode fiber, serialized by a multicore fiber delay line, and decoded by a deep learning model.
result: Achieves 100 MHz measurement rate with 0.32% mean relative error, a five-order-of-magnitude speed improvement over standard cameras.
conclusion: This spatial-to-temporal mapping paradigm enables real-time adaptive control and study of complex multimode nonlinear physics.

title: Smooth Hard-Thresholding For Singular Values With Stein's Unbiased Risk Estimate
authors: Guanzhong Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06632v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-rank matrix denoising is a central primitive in patch-based image restoration and many other inverse problems. Classical SVD-based image denoising methods often choose a truncation rank by matching residual singular-value energy with an estimated noise energy, but this rule is not a finite-sample risk principle because a fitted low-rank approximation inevitably absorbs part of the noise. This paper develops a mathematically rigorous alternative based on Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE). Since singular value hard thresholding is discontinuous and does not satisfy the hypotheses of Stein's lemma, we introduce a logistic smooth hard-threshold spectral estimator. We prove that the smooth shrinker satisfies the regularity conditions required by a spectral-estimator version of Stein's lemma, and therefore admits an exactly unbiased fixed-threshold risk estimate under Gaussian noise. For a fixed observed matrix and a finite set of candidate thresholds separated from the observed singular values, the ordering of the fixed-threshold smooth SURE objective eventually agrees with a simple limiting score. The limiting score has the same algebraic form as the biased hard-threshold SURE formula, but here it is used only as a computational device for ranking finite candidates. Selecting the minimizing threshold is a data-adaptive tuning step; the selected SURE value should not be interpreted as an unbiased risk estimate of the finally selected estimator.
tldr: This paper develops a smooth hard-thresholding estimator for singular values in low-rank matrix denoising, using Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE) for threshold selection.
motivation: Classical SVD-based denoising methods lack a finite-sample risk principle because the fitted low-rank approximation absorbs noise. The authors aim to provide a mathematically rigorous alternative.
method: They introduce a logistic smooth hard-threshold spectral estimator that satisfies Stein's lemma regularity conditions, enabling an unbiased risk estimate for fixed thresholds. They also derive a limiting score for ranking candidate thresholds.
result: The smooth SURE objective eventually agrees with a simple limiting score for finite candidate thresholds, and the minimizing threshold can be selected data-adaptively.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a principled approach to threshold selection in low-rank matrix denoising, though the selected SURE value is not an unbiased estimate of the final estimator's risk.

title: Spectral And Essential Spectral Analysis Of Finite-Rank Perturbations Of Unbounded Diagonal Operators On Non-Archimedean Hilbert Spaces
authors: Teylama Miabey
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the spectral properties of a class of unbounded linear operators on a non-Archimedean Hilbert space [MATH]. More precisely, we consider operators of the form \[ T=D+F,\qquad F=\sum_{j=1}^{m} u_j\otimes v_j, \] where [MATH] is an unbounded diagonal operator and [MATH] is a finite-rank perturbation. This work extends the spectral analysis of Diagana and McNeal for rank-one perturbations of diagonal operators to the case of arbitrary finite-rank perturbations. The main objective is to describe the spectrum, point spectrum, and essential spectrum of such operators in terms of the diagonal sequence associated with [MATH] and the Fredholm properties of [MATH]. The theory of Fredholm operators plays a central role, particularly in the computation of the essential spectrum and in the study of stability under finite-rank perturbations.
tldr: This paper studies spectral properties of finite-rank perturbations of unbounded diagonal operators on non-Archimedean Hilbert spaces, extending prior work to arbitrary finite-rank perturbations.
motivation: To generalize spectral analysis of rank-one perturbations to finite-rank perturbations in non-Archimedean Hilbert spaces, which is a purely mathematical topic.
method: Uses Fredholm operator theory to describe the spectrum, point spectrum, and essential spectrum in terms of the diagonal sequence and Fredholm properties.
result: Provides a description of the spectrum and essential spectrum for such operators, showing stability under finite-rank perturbations.
conclusion: The work extends known results to a more general setting, but remains within abstract functional analysis without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Environment-Division Multiple Access: An Enabler For AI-Native Multiple Access
authors: Zhiguo Ding
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, a new type of multiple access, termed Environment-Division Multiple Access (EDMA), is introduced and its interaction with AI-native communication networks is illustrated. In particular, the key properties of EDMA, such as utilizing the features of wireless propagation environments, integrating advanced flexible antennas, and proactively reconfiguring propagation environments, are described. The article also illustrates two types of applications of AI tools to multiple access, namely AI-assisted EDMA and AI-native EDMA. Finally, open problems and important directions for future research in AI-assisted EDMA are discussed.
tldr: This paper introduces Environment-Division Multiple Access (EDMA), a new multiple access technique for AI-native communication networks.
motivation: To address the need for efficient multiple access in future AI-native wireless networks by leveraging environmental features and reconfigurable propagation environments.
method: The paper describes the concept of EDMA, its key properties (utilizing wireless propagation environments, integrating advanced antennas, proactively reconfiguring environments), and discusses AI-assisted and AI-native EDMA approaches.
result: EDMA is proposed as a new multiple access paradigm that can be enhanced by AI tools, with open problems identified for future research.
conclusion: EDMA offers a promising direction for AI-native multiple access, but the paper is a conceptual overview without technical depth or experimental validation.

title: A Unified DeepONet Framework For Logarithmically Stable Infinite-Dimensional Inverse Problems
authors: Wen-Jie Wu, Tiexiang Li, Wen-Wei Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a unified DeepONet framework for logarithmically stable infinite-dimensional inverse problems, with inverse acoustic scattering as a model application. The framework is formulated at the operator level by separating the learned inverse map into measurement encoding, finite-dimensional neural approximation, and functional reconstruction components. For inverse maps satisfying a logarithmic stability estimate, we establish quantitative a priori error bounds giving separate estimates for the encoder error, the neural approximation error, and the reconstruction error, thereby characterizing the dependence on the encoder dimension, the network size, and the reconstruction dimension. For comparison, we also record the corresponding Lipschitz-stable estimate arising from the same error decomposition. The abstract theory is then specialized to the recovery of a medium contrast from fixed-frequency far-field measurements. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions illustrate stable reconstructions under measurement noise.
tldr: A unified DeepONet framework for logarithmically stable infinite-dimensional inverse problems, applied to inverse acoustic scattering.
motivation: Inverse problems often suffer from instability; the authors aim to develop a neural network framework that leverages logarithmic stability for robust reconstruction.
method: They propose a DeepONet-based architecture that separates the inverse map into measurement encoding, finite-dimensional neural approximation, and functional reconstruction, with theoretical error bounds.
result: Quantitative a priori error bounds are established, and numerical experiments in 2D and 3D demonstrate stable reconstructions under noise.
conclusion: The framework provides a principled approach to solving logarithmically stable inverse problems with neural networks, with potential extensions to other applications.

title: Numerical Approximation Of The Stochastic Cahn--Hilliard Equation With Singular Potential
authors: Stefan Metzger \v{l}ubom\'ir Ba\v{n}as
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07164v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss the numerical approximation of the stochastic Cahn--Hilliard equation with a singular double-obstacle potential and multiplicative conservative noise. We propose a regularised fully discrete finite element approximation scheme for the problem and show that it satisfies stability estimates which are uniform with respect to the discretization parameters. We show convergence of the approximation for vanishing discretization parameters towards a regularised version of the singular stochastic Cahn--Hilliard equation by monotonicity arguments. Hence, thanks to a uniform [MATH]-estimate for the regularised problem we show that the regularised solution converges towards the pathwise unique probabilistically strong solution of the original singular stochastic Cahn--Hilliard equation. We conclude by presenting numerical simulations where we compare the regularised numerical approximation to its unregularised counterpart and illustrate the effect of the conservative noise.
tldr: This paper develops a numerical approximation scheme for the stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation with a singular potential and multiplicative noise.
motivation: The stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation models phase separation under thermal fluctuations, but its singular potential poses numerical challenges.
method: A regularized finite element scheme is proposed, with stability and convergence proofs via monotonicity and uniform estimates.
result: The regularized approximation converges to the unique strong solution of the original singular equation as discretization parameters vanish.
conclusion: The scheme is effective for simulating the stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation with singular potentials, as demonstrated by numerical experiments.

title: Enhancing Malware Detection With Generative Ai: Using Variational Autoencoders To Boost Machine Learning Classifiers' Performance
authors: Jeremy Straub Mohammad Alharbi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The advancement of malware poses obstacles for cybersecurity, necessitating the development of advanced detection techniques. This paper proposes an approach to enhance malware detection through the use of a generative artificial intelligence model. Specifically, variational autoencoders (VAEs) are used with the random forest, XGBoost and sequential model machine learning classifiers. Generated synthetic malware samples are used to address the critical issue of data scarcity for new or less common malware types. This approach can be used to augment datasets to improve classifier robustness. The proposed methodology uses VAEs to create high-quality diverse synthetic datasets that closely mimic real-world malware data. The effectiveness of these augmented datasets is evaluated by comparing the performance of the machine learning classifiers when they are trained with the original data and when they are trained with the synthetic data-augmented datasets. The results demonstrate a notable improvement in the accuracy, precision, recall and F1-scores of the classifiers, when they are trained using the augmented datasets. The enhanced performance for detecting various malware classes shows the potential of this approach to facilitate adaptation to evolving malware threats effectively. This work demonstrates the utility of generative AI for cybersecurity. It also provides a foundation for future research aimed at developing more resilient and adaptive malware detection systems.
tldr: This paper uses variational autoencoders to generate synthetic malware samples for augmenting training data, improving machine learning classifiers for malware detection.
motivation: Malware detection faces data scarcity for new or rare malware types, limiting classifier robustness.
method: Variational autoencoders generate synthetic malware samples; these augment original datasets to train random forest, XGBoost, and sequential models.
result: Augmented datasets improve accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-scores across classifiers for various malware classes.
conclusion: Generative AI can enhance malware detection by addressing data imbalance and improving classifier adaptability to evolving threats.

title: Evidence Markets
authors: Safwan Hossain, Gabriel Andrade, Chengqi Zang, Yiling Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern prediction markets face two limitations that restrict their applicability in a range of settings:~(i)~they reveal what the crowd believes but not the evidence or reasoning behind those beliefs, and~(ii)~they require an event with an external ground truth that resolves at a known future date. We address these twin challenges by introducing evidence markets, a generalization of prediction markets that incentivizes the submission of evidence alongside beliefs and can be endogenously resolved using the crowd-sourced evidence if external resolution is not possible. At its core, the market uses a logarithmic market scoring rule whose liquidity parameter changes dynamically with the accumulated evidence quality. We prove that platform loss is bounded, evidence is rewarded proportional to the current market uncertainty, and can be equivalently implemented through an automated market maker. In the case where the marker resolves endogenously based on submitted evidence, we characterize how withholding evidence shifts a trader's belief about resolution and use it to prove truthful belief and evidence reporting is a always an [MATH]-dominant strategy incentive compatible (DSIC) strategy. To address operational considerations, we propose evidence verification via an LLM-as-a-Judge framework with staking and give an asynchronous execution algorithm that is not bottle-necked by verification. Throughout the work, we use LLM evaluations -- determining which model is best for a given task -- as a salient and representative running example for our proposed market.
tldr: Introduces evidence markets, a generalization of prediction markets that incentivizes submission of evidence and can resolve endogenously using crowd-sourced evidence.
motivation: Modern prediction markets reveal beliefs but not evidence, and require external ground truth; evidence markets address these limitations.
method: Uses a logarithmic market scoring rule with dynamic liquidity parameter based on accumulated evidence quality; proposes LLM-as-a-Judge for evidence verification.
result: Proves bounded platform loss, evidence reward proportional to uncertainty, and truthful reporting as a DSIC strategy under endogenous resolution.
conclusion: Evidence markets can elicit both beliefs and evidence, with applications in LLM evaluation and other settings lacking external ground truth.

title: Rational Heun Operators On $q$-linear Grids
authors: Satoshi Tsujimoto, Luc Vinet, Alexei Zhedanov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rational Heun operators on the [MATH]linear grid are presented. They are second-order [MATH]difference operators [MATH] constructively defined from the requirement that they have a raising action on rational functions of type [MATH], namely [MATH], with poles on [MATH]linear grids. It will be observed that these operators are related to one family of the Ruijsenaars-van Diejen-Takemura Hamiltonians. A distinguished subclass of [MATH] called classical which shifts the pole structure while preserving the rational function type and a prescribed basis is also characterized.
tldr: The paper introduces rational Heun operators on q-linear grids and relates them to Ruijsenaars-van Diejen-Takemura Hamiltonians.
motivation: To construct and characterize rational Heun operators on q-linear grids, which are second-order difference operators with raising action on rational functions.
method: The operators are defined constructively from the requirement of raising action on rational functions with poles on q-linear grids, and a subclass called classical is characterized.
result: The operators are related to one family of Ruijsenaars-van Diejen-Takemura Hamiltonians, and a distinguished classical subclass is identified.
conclusion: The work provides a new class of difference operators with potential applications in special functions and integrable systems.

title: Impact Of Capacity Volatility And Input Substitutability On Supply Chain Resilience
authors: Jaeseok Hur, Juha Jang, Meesoon Ha, Hawoong Jeong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Supply chains are intrinsically vulnerable to stochastic shocks due to their sequential production dependencies. Building on the Feld-Barthelemy framework, we investigate how capacity volatility and input substitutability determine critical demands in stochastic supply chains. By modeling production capacity with a truncated normal distribution, we show that in long supply chains, reducing capacity volatility is often more effective than increasing average capacity, emphasizing the need for firm-level synchronization. Furthermore, introducing a modified Leontief-type production function reveals that input substitutability effectively disperses stochastic shocks. Supplier diversification inherently raises critical demands, even under fixed maximum capacities, by introducing the effect of network topology that independently enhances the resilience of physical stock. Our findings demonstrate that mitigating capacity volatility and structurally diversifying supply routes are just as crucial to supply chain resilience as traditional inventory expansion.
tldr: This paper studies supply chain resilience under stochastic shocks using a modified Feld-Barthelemy framework, focusing on capacity volatility and input substitutability.
motivation: Supply chains are vulnerable to disruptions; understanding how capacity volatility and input substitutability affect critical demand thresholds can inform resilience strategies.
method: The authors model production capacity with a truncated normal distribution and introduce a modified Leontief-type production function to analyze the effects of volatility and substitutability on critical demands.
result: Reducing capacity volatility is more effective than increasing average capacity in long supply chains, and input substitutability disperses shocks, while supplier diversification raises critical demands.
conclusion: Mitigating capacity volatility and diversifying supply routes are crucial for supply chain resilience, complementing traditional inventory expansion.

title: Generalized Analytical Relations To Describe Global Optical Systems With A Plenoptic Camera
authors: Marc Brunel, Pierre Schleuniger, Adrian Marszalek, Valentin Muset, Ramana Kukkarasi, S\'ebastien Coetmellec, Jean-Bernard Blaisot
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The optical transfer matrix formalism is used to describe global set-ups incorporating a plenoptic camera. Analytical relations that give the effective resolution, depth of field, disparity and optimum patch size for image reconstruction are established versus the optical parameters of any global arrangement. The potentiality of this formulation is illustrated analyzing experimental results obtained in astigmatic cylindrical imaging conditions.
tldr: This paper uses the optical transfer matrix formalism to derive analytical relations for plenoptic camera systems, focusing on resolution, depth of field, and disparity.
motivation: To provide a unified analytical framework for designing and characterizing plenoptic camera setups, which are used in light-field imaging.
method: The authors apply the optical transfer matrix formalism to model global optical systems incorporating a plenoptic camera, deriving analytical expressions for key imaging parameters.
result: Analytical relations for effective resolution, depth of field, disparity, and optimum patch size are established and validated with experimental data from astigmatic cylindrical imaging.
conclusion: The proposed formalism enables systematic design and analysis of plenoptic imaging systems, with potential applications in computational photography and 3D imaging.

title: Einstein-Kropina Metrics And Their Application In Finsler Gravity
authors: Sjors Heefer, Fidel F. Villase\~nor, Andrea Fuster
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We generalize the Einstein condition for Kropina metrics obtained in the positive definite setting by Zhang, Shen and others to all signatures. As examples of Einstein-Kropina metrics [MATH], we construct new explicit positive definite ones and the first ones with Lorentzian signature. Next, we classify all Einstein-Kropina solutions to the vacuum equation of Finsler gravity by Pfeifer and Wohlfarth, in arbitrary dimension and including a possible cosmological constant [MATH]. For the Lorentzian and positive definite cases, the local picture is as follows. In dimension 4 or lower, only the trivial solution exists: a Minkowski or Euclidean space, essentially. In dimension 5 and higher, the solutions are those [MATH] for which the metric [MATH] is a product of the real line with a Ricci-flat metric (Lorentzian or Riemannian) and the vector field [MATH] is the unique unit vector on the first factor. As a very surprising rigidity phenomenon, all Einstein-Kropina solutions to the [MATH]-vacuum equation are Berwald and Ricci-flat, and the cosmological constant necessarily vanishes.
tldr: This paper generalizes Einstein-Kropina metrics to arbitrary signatures and classifies solutions to Finsler gravity vacuum equations, revealing a rigidity phenomenon.
motivation: To extend the study of Einstein-Kropina metrics beyond positive definite signatures and to classify all solutions of Finsler gravity vacuum equations.
method: The authors generalize the Einstein condition for Kropina metrics to all signatures, construct explicit examples, and classify solutions to the vacuum equation of Finsler gravity using mathematical analysis.
result: New explicit Einstein-Kropina metrics are constructed, including the first Lorentzian examples. In dimension ≤4 only trivial Minkowski/Euclidean solutions exist; in higher dimensions solutions are product metrics with a Ricci-flat factor and a unit vector field. All solutions are Berwald and Ricci-flat with vanishing cosmological constant.
conclusion: The paper presents a complete classification of Einstein-Kropina solutions to Finsler gravity, showing strong rigidity and no nontrivial solutions in low dimensions.

title: When Infinity Stopped Being Embarrassing: The Doubly Infinite Series Of Pierre Alphonse Laurent And The Mathematical Rehabilitation Of Singularities
authors: N. Karjanto B. Sriraman
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the better part of a century, isolated singularities were treated as pathological obstructions requiring elaborate avoidance strategies. Pierre Alphonse Laurent (1813--1854), a French military engineer at Le Havre, ended this avoidance in 1843 by extending Cauchy's Taylor-type theorem to doubly connected (annular) domains, producing the doubly infinite power series that now bears his name. Negative-power terms in the expansion encode precise geometric information about the singularity rather than signaling a breakdown of the formalism. Laurent's contribution arrived through an unhappy institutional trajectory -- submitted after a prize deadline, subjected to a priority claim by Cauchy, and issued in full only posthumously in 1863 -- yet it became indispensable to every branch of mathematics and mathematical physics that touches on complex function theory. We reconstruct the mathematical problem Laurent solved, place it within Cauchy's analytic program of the 1830s--1840s, examine the institutional failure that prevented publication, document the independent parallel proof by Weierstrass (1841, published 1894), and trace the series' absorption into the standard toolkit via Briot and Bouquet and the residue calculus. Drawing on Laurent's 1843 Comptes rendus notice, Cauchy's Academy report, Bertrand's memorial notice (1890), and the secondary literature (Neuenschwander 1978, 1981; Manning 1975; Bottazzini 1986; Gray 2015), we analyze the philosophical significance of the series, which we term ``exile mathematics'', and survey its reach into perturbation theory, number theory, probability, and quantum field theory. Readers familiar with the theorem but not its institutional history will find here a documented account of why a foundational result was withheld for two decades and how it nevertheless achieved canonical status.
tldr: A historical and philosophical account of Pierre Alphonse Laurent's doubly infinite series and its impact on complex analysis.
motivation: To document the institutional and mathematical history behind the Laurent series, which was delayed in publication due to priority disputes and Cauchy's influence.
method: Historical reconstruction using primary sources (Laurent's 1843 notice, Cauchy's report, Bertrand's memorial) and secondary literature.
result: The Laurent series became a fundamental tool in complex analysis, perturbation theory, number theory, probability, and quantum field theory.
conclusion: The paper highlights how a foundational mathematical result overcame institutional obstacles to achieve canonical status.

title: Dense Signed Sums Of Non-integer Powers
authors: David Treeby
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that if [MATH] is not an integer, then there is a choice of signs [MATH] such that the partial sums [MATH] are dense in [MATH]. The proof groups consecutive terms into Thue--Morse blocks, whose Prouhet--Tarry--Escott cancellation produces nonzero block sums tending to zero but with divergent total variation. A standard steering argument then chooses block signs so that the resulting partial sums visit arbitrarily small neighbourhoods of every real number.
tldr: The paper proves that for any non-integer exponent, there exists a sign assignment making partial sums of the series dense in the real line.
motivation: To understand the density properties of signed sums of non-integer powers, extending known results for integer exponents.
method: Groups terms into Thue-Morse blocks, uses Prouhet-Tarry-Escott cancellation to produce small nonzero block sums with divergent total variation, then applies a steering argument to choose block signs.
result: For any non-integer exponent, the partial sums can be made dense in ℝ.
conclusion: The result demonstrates a striking density property for non-integer power series with appropriate sign choices.

title: Multipliers Of Beurling-Fourier Algebras
authors: Mahmood Alaghmandan, Olof Giselsson, Ebrahim Samei, Lyudmila Turowska
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a locally compact group G we introduce and study the reduced Beurling-Fourier-Stieltjes algebra, a weighted analogue of the reduced Fourier-Stieltjes algebra, together with the algebra of completely bounded multipliers of the associated weighted Fourier algebra. We show, in particular, that these two algebras coincide when G is amenable. For a general locally compact group G, we identify them as subspaces of the reduced Fourier-Stieltjes algebra and of the space of functions that locally belong to the Fourier algebra, respectively. Furthermore, we establish sufficient conditions on the group and the weight under which the algebra of completely bounded multipliers of the weighted Fourier algebra embeds into its unweighted counterpart.
tldr: This paper studies multipliers of Beurling-Fourier algebras on locally compact groups, a topic in abstract harmonic analysis.
motivation: To understand the structure of weighted Fourier algebras and their multiplier algebras, particularly for amenable groups.
method: Uses functional analysis and group theory to define and compare reduced Beurling-Fourier-Stieltjes algebras and completely bounded multipliers.
result: Shows that for amenable groups, the two algebras coincide, and identifies them as subspaces of the reduced Fourier-Stieltjes algebra.
conclusion: Provides conditions under which the completely bounded multiplier algebra embeds into its unweighted counterpart.

title: High-order Conforming Finite Elements For The Cahn-Hilliard Equation: Relative-energy Stability And Energy Defects
authors: Marvin Fritz Aaron Brunk
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a semidiscrete single-field Galerkin approximation of the Cahn-Hilliard equation using high-order conforming finite element spaces. More specifically, globally [MATH] finite elements with [MATH]-conforming trial spaces, including Argyris, Bell, and Bogner-Fox-Schmit elements, allow a direct discretization of the fourth-order formulation and preserve mass exactly. The main structural result is an exact energy balance for the physical Cahn-Hilliard energy. Besides the expected discrete dissipation, the balance contains an explicitly computable energy defect. This defect vanishes for Laplacian-invariant periodic spaces, such as Fourier spaces, but is generally nonzero for classical [MATH] finite elements. It therefore quantifies the precise loss of a discrete gradient-flow structure. We prove semidiscrete a priori error estimates by a relative-energy argument. The estimate is closed using an augmented relative energy and a discrete elliptic reconstruction bound for the inverse discrete Laplacian. The resulting convergence rates match the expected approximation orders. Numerical experiments with Bell and Argyris elements confirm the rates and demonstrate the defect mechanism by comparison with a Fourier reference discretization.
tldr: This paper studies high-order conforming finite element methods for the Cahn-Hilliard equation, focusing on energy stability and discretization error.
motivation: To develop and analyze finite element discretizations that preserve the gradient-flow structure of the Cahn-Hilliard equation, quantifying the energy defect introduced by non-periodic boundary conditions.
method: Uses Argyris, Bell, and Bogner-Fox-Schmit elements for direct discretization of the fourth-order PDE, and derives a relative-energy stability estimate with an augmented relative energy and discrete elliptic reconstruction.
result: Proves an exact energy balance with a computable energy defect, and establishes semidiscrete a priori error estimates that match expected approximation orders.
conclusion: The proposed finite element methods achieve optimal convergence rates while preserving mass exactly, but the energy defect reveals a loss of the discrete gradient-flow structure for non-periodic spaces.

title: A Spectral-Based Method For Network-Formation PDEs
authors: Pedro Aceves-Sanchez, Pierre Degond, Sara Merino-Aceituno, Claudia Wytrzens
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose and study a simple and scalable Fourier-based spectral method for a continuum model of network formation under periodic boundary conditions. The model provides the evolution of the pressure [MATH] and the conductivity [MATH] over time. The evolution of [MATH] is given by an anisotropic Poisson equation, while the equation for [MATH] contains three terms corresponding to a diffusion and an activation term of the network -- that depends on the gradient of the pressure -- as well as a relaxation term that acts as a decaying term. This system arises as a formal [MATH]-gradient flow of a non-convex energy functional. Our algorithm combines two ingredients: (i) a splitting method for the equation for [MATH], where the activation and relaxation parts are solved analytically, and the diffusion part is solved via Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), and (ii) an FFT combined with the Conjugate Gradient (CG) method applied to the equation for the pressure. This makes the scheme easy to implement compared to implicit schemes and naturally extensible to three dimensions on uniform periodic grids. To showcase the method, we recover the previously documented influence of the activation strength [MATH], the diffusion coefficient [MATH], and the metabolic exponent [MATH] on the morphology of emergent networks, and report grid convergence results.
tldr: This paper proposes a Fourier-based spectral method for solving a continuum model of network formation, which is a PDE system describing pressure and conductivity evolution.
motivation: To develop a simple, scalable, and easy-to-implement numerical method for simulating network formation PDEs, avoiding the complexity of implicit schemes.
method: The algorithm combines operator splitting for the conductivity equation (solving activation and relaxation analytically, diffusion via FFT) and an FFT-conjugate gradient method for the pressure equation.
result: The method recovers known morphological effects of activation strength, diffusion coefficient, and metabolic exponent on emergent networks, and demonstrates grid convergence.
conclusion: The spectral method is effective and extensible to 3D, providing a practical tool for studying network formation dynamics.

title: Linear Poroelasticity With Solid Incompressibility: Consistent Formulation And Scalable Numerical Solution
authors: Nicol\'as A. Barnafi, Andr\'es E. Rubiano, Ricardo Ruiz-Baier
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we propose, by linearizing the equations of fully nonlinear poroelasticity, a consistent model in which only the solid phase is incompressible. This reformulation circumvents some inconsistency issues encountered in standard primal formulations of nonlinear poroelasticity while still retaining its key physical coupling mechanisms. We show a well-posed and consistent discretization strategy and also formulate scalable solvers based on a Schur complement formalism. A distinctive feature of the model is that it allows for a lowest order, inf-sup stable family of Finite Elements (FE) spaces. Numerical tests in two and three dimensions are provided to validate the proposed method and solver framework.
tldr: This paper presents a consistent formulation and scalable numerical solution for linear poroelasticity with solid incompressibility.
motivation: Standard primal formulations of nonlinear poroelasticity suffer from inconsistency issues; a consistent model is needed that retains key physical coupling mechanisms.
method: The authors linearize the fully nonlinear poroelasticity equations, propose a well-posed discretization using inf-sup stable finite elements, and develop scalable solvers based on a Schur complement formalism.
result: The model allows lowest-order, inf-sup stable finite element spaces, and numerical tests in 2D and 3D validate the method and solver framework.
conclusion: The proposed formulation resolves inconsistency issues and provides a scalable numerical approach for linear poroelasticity with solid incompressibility.

title: A Primal--Dual Penalty Algorithm And Optimal Control Of The Double Integrator
authors: Regina S. Burachik, C. Yal\c{c}{\i}n Kaya, Xuemei Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the behaviour of a primal--dual penalty scheme applied to all possible instances, i.e., boundary conditions, of an optimal control problem involving the double integrator. The proposed duality-based framework enables us to derive closed-form expressions for the associated dual functions as well as for the optimal control variables. Furthermore, we provide a complete characterization of the least exact penalty parameter for this problem. The iteration dynamics of the algorithm are examined by constructing and analyzing the trajectories of the constraint functions for every admissible instance of the problem. Finally, we compare the two step-size rules employed in our primal--dual algorithm with two alternative Polyak-type step-size strategies.
tldr: This paper studies a primal-dual penalty algorithm for optimal control of the double integrator, a classical problem in control theory.
motivation: To analyze the behavior of a primal-dual penalty scheme for all boundary conditions of the double integrator optimal control problem and to characterize the least exact penalty parameter.
method: The authors derive closed-form expressions for dual functions and optimal control variables using a duality-based framework, and examine iteration dynamics by constructing constraint trajectories.
result: Complete characterization of the least exact penalty parameter and comparison of two step-size rules with Polyak-type strategies.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a thorough analysis of the primal-dual penalty algorithm for this specific control problem.

title: The Sharp Phase Transition Of Tyler's M-Estimator For Robust Subspace Recovery
authors: Teng Zhang Gilad Lerman
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robust Subspace Recovery (RSR) aims to identify an underlying d-dimensional subspace from a dataset heavily corrupted by outliers. Complexity-theoretic results establish a threshold for the problem's computational hardness based on the dimension-scaled signal-to-noise ratio (DS-SNR): the problem is SSE-hard when the DS-SNR is strictly less than 1, and solvable via practical algorithms when it is greater than 1 under general position assumptions. However, the exact behavior of practical algorithms at the critical boundary DS-SNR = 1 has remained unknown. This work resolves the behavior of Tyler's M-estimator (TME) at this critical boundary, consequently establishing a sharp phase transition. Specifically, we prove that TME converges exactly to the true subspace for DS-SNR \geq 1 under a new stability condition, which is less restrictive than the general position assumptions used in prior literature. Our analysis utilizes a decomposition of the TME iterates within a majorization-minimization framework.
tldr: This paper proves a sharp phase transition for Tyler's M-estimator in robust subspace recovery at the critical DS-SNR threshold.
motivation: Robust subspace recovery is a fundamental problem in statistics and machine learning, and understanding the exact behavior of practical algorithms at the computational hardness threshold is important.
method: The authors analyze Tyler's M-estimator using a majorization-minimization framework and decompose its iterates to prove convergence under a new stability condition.
result: They show that Tyler's M-estimator converges exactly to the true subspace when the dimension-scaled signal-to-noise ratio is at least 1, under a less restrictive condition than previous work.
conclusion: This resolves the behavior of Tyler's M-estimator at the critical boundary, establishing a sharp phase transition for robust subspace recovery.

title: Dynamics And Structure Of Pull-in And Touchdown Behavior In Parallel-plate Electrostatic Mems Actuators Via Geometric Approaches
authors: Yu Ichida, Kyoichi Kakuno, Daisuke Yamane
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper focuses on parallel-plate electrostatic actuators, which are fundamental structures found in Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) for numerous modern devices. It considers the equations used to model these actuators. In particular, we investigate the behavior of the solutions to a MEMS model that is represented by a second-order ordinary differential equation, where the spring is characterized as soft, linear, or hard. We present the mathematical structure underlying the pull-in and touchdown phenomena that characterize the behavior of systems incorporating soft and hard spring, based on the behavior of linear springs. The pull-in phenomenon corresponds to the degeneration of the solutions to the model equation. The touchdown phenomenon corresponds to the finite-time singularity of the solutions. These global dynamics and structures are systematically revealed through geometric approaches based on Poincar\'e-type compactification, the center manifold theorem, and blow-up technique. These methods successfully induce and resolve the dynamics at infinity.
tldr: This paper analyzes pull-in and touchdown dynamics in MEMS actuators using geometric methods.
motivation: Understanding the nonlinear dynamics of electrostatic MEMS actuators is important for device design and reliability.
method: The authors use Poincaré-type compactification, center manifold theorem, and blow-up technique to study the global dynamics of a second-order ODE model.
result: They systematically reveal the mathematical structure underlying pull-in and touchdown phenomena for soft, linear, and hard springs.
conclusion: The geometric approach successfully characterizes the singular behavior of the MEMS model, providing insights into actuator failure mechanisms.

title: Adaptive Multiscale Model Reduction For Linear Elasticity Equation In Perforated Domains
authors: Wei Xie, Eric Chung, Yin Yang, Yunqing Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a Constraint Energy Minimizing Generalized Multiscale Finite Element Method (CEM-GMsFEM) for solving linear elasticity problems in heterogeneous perforated domains. The presence of numerous perforations introduces multiple scales into the computational domain, making direct fine-grid simulations computationally expensive. The proposed method follows the standard offline--online decomposition of CEM-GMsFEM. In the offline stage, local spectral problems are solved on coarse elements to construct auxiliary spaces, and localized energy-minimizing basis functions are then computed on oversampled regions to capture fine-scale geometric information induced by the perforations. In the online stage, residual-driven basis functions are constructed in enlarged coarse neighborhoods to incorporate source-term information and improve the accuracy of the multiscale approximation adaptively. We establish convergence results for both the offline and online stages. In particular, we derive error estimates for the localized multiscale approximation and prove the convergence of the adaptive online enrichment algorithm. Moreover, we show that the oversampling regions used in the online stage can be determined locally, leading to a reduction in computational cost while maintaining convergence properties. Numerical experiments on perforated media with different geometric configurations demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper develops a multiscale finite element method for linear elasticity in perforated domains, focusing on computational efficiency and error bounds.
motivation: Direct fine-grid simulations of linear elasticity in heterogeneous perforated domains are computationally expensive due to multiple scales introduced by perforations.
method: The method uses Constraint Energy Minimizing Generalized Multiscale Finite Element Method (CEM-GMsFEM) with offline construction of localized basis functions and online residual-driven enrichment.
result: Convergence results and error estimates are established for both offline and online stages, and numerical experiments demonstrate accuracy and efficiency.
conclusion: The proposed adaptive multiscale method effectively reduces computational cost while maintaining accuracy for linear elasticity in perforated domains.

title: Weighted Sum-Rate Enhancement For Flexible Intelligent Metasurface-Assisted Multicell Systems
authors: Hanwen Hu, Jiancheng An, Lu Gan, Hongbin Li, Naofal Al-Dhahir, George K. Karagiannidis, Arumugam Nallanathan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Flexible intelligent metasurface (FIM) technology has emerged as a promising technology for enhancing wireless communication performance by dynamically reshaping the propagation environment. Compared with conventional rigid reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), an FIM is composed of multiple electromagnetic (EM) scattering units, each of which can flexibly modify its displacement in the direction normal to the surface, thereby cooperatively morphing the overall surface shape. This additional degree of freedom (DoF) enables improved beamforming and interference mitigation, particularly in complex multicell scenarios. In this paper, an optimization problem for maximizing the weighted sum-rate (WSR) in a multicell multi-user multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) system assisted by an FIM deployed at the cell boundary is investigated. We jointly optimize the transmit beamforming at the base station (BS), the phase shift matrix, and the FIM surface shape, subject to constraints on the transmit power budget, unit-modulus reflection coefficients, and surface shape morphing range. Due to the non-convex objective function with highly coupled variables, solving the formulated optimization problem is challenging. To tackle this challenge, we propose an efficient alternating optimization framework that leverages the weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) method to reformulate the problem and the block coordinate descent (BCD) algorithm to iteratively update the variables. Specifically, the Riemannian conjugate gradient (RCG) algorithm is leveraged to optimize the phase shift matrix, while the projected gradient descent (PGD) method is adopted to optimize the surface shape of the FIM. Additionally, the optimal beamforming vectors are obtained in closed form.
tldr: This paper proposes an optimization framework for weighted sum-rate enhancement in multicell wireless systems using flexible intelligent metasurfaces.
motivation: To improve wireless communication performance in complex multicell scenarios by leveraging the additional degrees of freedom provided by flexible intelligent metasurfaces.
method: Joint optimization of transmit beamforming, phase shifts, and surface shape using alternating optimization with WMMSE, BCD, RCG, and PGD algorithms.
result: The proposed framework achieves enhanced weighted sum-rate compared to conventional rigid RIS systems.
conclusion: Flexible intelligent metasurfaces offer significant performance gains for multicell MU-MISO systems through optimized surface morphing.

title: Successive Convexification For Trajectory Optimization With Continuous-time Satisfaction Of Signal Temporal Logic Specifications
authors: Beh\c{c}et A\c{c}{\i}kme\c{s}e Samet Uzun
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a successive convexification framework for trajectory optimization under continuous-time Signal Temporal Logic (CT-STL) specifications. The framework employs generalized mean-based robustness (GMSR), a smooth and exact parameterization of discrete-time STL, as a logical building block for constructing differentiable CT-STL constraints in optimal control. It is integrated with time-dilation for free-final-time problems, finite-dimensional control parameterization, multiple-shooting discretization of the dynamics, and a convergence-guaranteed sequential convex programming method, prox-convex, to solve the nonconvex program. The main CT-STL realization embeds temporal aggregation into augmented continuous-time dynamics. This augmentation-based construction is largely transcription-independent, can be incorporated into existing optimal-control pipelines with minimal structural changes, and enables smooth CT-STL parameterizations with accuracy controlled by a user-selected regularization parameter. We also discuss a complementary dense-time realization that evaluates CT-STL formulas directly on the integration subnodes used for dynamics discretization, yielding a smooth and exact parameterization on the numerical trajectory representation, up to the accuracy of the integration scheme. The proposed GMSR-based formulations mitigate the locality and gradient-masking behavior of standard quantitative semantics and therefore provide a favorable landscape for gradient-based trajectory optimization. The framework is demonstrated through trajectory-optimization examples for a double-integrator system with continuous-time \always{}, \eventually{}, and \until{} specifications, and a 6-DoF quadrotor flight problem with combined \always{}, \implication{}, and \eventually{}-type specifications. The implementation is available at [URL].
tldr: This paper presents a successive convexification framework for trajectory optimization with continuous-time Signal Temporal Logic specifications.
motivation: To enable trajectory optimization that satisfies complex temporal logic constraints in continuous time, which is important for autonomous systems.
method: The framework uses generalized mean-based robustness (GMSR) to create differentiable CT-STL constraints, integrates time-dilation, control parameterization, multiple-shooting, and a prox-convex sequential convex programming method.
result: The approach is demonstrated on double-integrator and quadrotor examples, showing effective satisfaction of CT-STL specifications.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a transcription-independent way to incorporate CT-STL constraints into optimal control pipelines with favorable optimization landscapes.

title: Scalable Finite Adaptability Via Polyhedral Partition And Learning
authors: Zolykha Rezaei, Ningji Wei, Eojin Han
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite adaptability for decision-making under uncertainty, where a small set of candidate solutions is prepared in advance and the best response is selected after uncertainty is realized. While existing methods have made significant progress on exact formulations, scalability remains a persistent challenge due to (i) the combinatorial nature of assigning decisions to uncertainty realizations, and (ii) the joint optimization of uncertainty set partition and subsequent decisions. We propose a framework that makes the partition of the uncertainty set explicit and uses polyhedral partitions as the basis for policy design. Under mild regularity conditions and for general risk measures, we show that such policies converge to the optimal fully adjustable policy as the number of regions increases. Building on this result, we develop a parametric partition framework that allows flexible policy design with tractable reformulations for both robust and stochastic finite adaptability problems. To improve scalability, we introduce an approximate-learn-parallel framework that integrates partition learning with parallel optimization while preserving solution robustness. Computational experiments on classical testbeds in both robust and stochastic settings show that the proposed method scales to larger instances and yields competitive policy performance.
tldr: This paper proposes a scalable finite adaptability framework for decision-making under uncertainty using polyhedral partitions and learning, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Existing finite adaptability methods face scalability challenges due to combinatorial assignment and joint optimization of partition and decisions.
method: The framework uses explicit polyhedral partitions of the uncertainty set, parametric partition design, and an approximate-learn-parallel approach integrating partition learning with parallel optimization.
result: The method scales to larger instances and yields competitive policy performance on classical robust and stochastic optimization testbeds.
conclusion: Polyhedral partition-based finite adaptability with learning can achieve scalability while preserving solution robustness.

title: A Single-Loop Regularized Newton Method For Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization
authors: Bohao Ma, Nachuan Xiao, Junyu Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For smooth nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax problems, existing second-order methods share a common double-loop structure where the inner maximization is solved to sufficiently high accuracy before each second-order step. First-order methods are often adopted in the inner loops for scalability, but they also undermine the condition-insensitivity of second-order methods, limiting these methods to instances with mild conditioning. To resolve this issue, we propose a novel single-loop framework based on an equivalent regularized minimization reformulation of the original problem. By deriving a new adaptive cubic-quadratic majorization to dynamically absorb the non-Lipschitz components of the reformulated Hessian, we establish a regularized Newton method with robust theoretical guarantees across multiple settings. For deterministic problems, our single-loop method matches the [MATH] global iteration complexity of the existing double-loop second-order methods, while automatically achieving a local superlinear rate that is unavailable in existing works due to the inner-loop bottleneck. For the stochastic setting, we achieve [MATH] gradient and [MATH] Hessian complexities by integrating a recursive variance reduction, strictly improving those of the double-loop methods by [MATH] factors. In both deterministic and stochastic experiments, our methods significantly outperform the benchmarks, offering substantial speedups over the double-loop methods even under mildly conditioned instances. As a byproduct of our analysis, we close a gap in stochastic second-order methods for nonconvex minimization, where the best known result contains a nontrivial technical issue.
tldr: This paper proposes a single-loop regularized Newton method for nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax optimization, achieving improved complexity bounds and local superlinear convergence.
motivation: Existing second-order methods for minimax problems use double-loop structures that require solving inner maximization accurately, limiting scalability and conditioning insensitivity.
method: The authors reformulate the minimax problem as a regularized minimization and derive an adaptive cubic-quadratic majorization to handle non-Lipschitz Hessian components, enabling a single-loop regularized Newton method.
result: The method matches global iteration complexity of double-loop methods, achieves local superlinear convergence, and improves gradient/Hessian complexities in the stochastic setting by factors of O(κ^2) and O(κ^2) respectively.
conclusion: The proposed single-loop framework overcomes the inner-loop bottleneck of double-loop methods, offering substantial speedups in both deterministic and stochastic experiments.

title: Integral Stochastic Orders Of $m$-generalized Order Statistics From Transform-ordered Nonparametric Families
authors: Idir Arab, Tommaso Lando, Paulo Eduardo Oliveira, Tomasz Rychlik
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide sufficient conditions for comparing [MATH]-generalized order statistics with respect to the increasing concave, increasing convex, and star-shaped stochastic orders. These conditions allow us to rank classical order statistics, selected censored type-II order statistics, and records. They depend on both the parameters of the generalized order statistics and the underlying distribution. Rather than assuming a specific parametric form, we adopt a nonparametric approach and assume some stochastic transform-ordered property, that is, some suitable shape condition. This framework encompasses many relevant classes of distributions that are related, via transform order, to the generalized and the negative generalized Pareto distribution.
tldr: This paper studies integral stochastic orders for m-generalized order statistics under transform-ordered nonparametric families.
motivation: To provide sufficient conditions for comparing generalized order statistics with respect to various stochastic orders without assuming a specific parametric form.
method: The authors adopt a nonparametric approach assuming stochastic transform-ordered properties, which encompass classes related to generalized Pareto distributions.
result: Conditions are derived that allow ranking classical order statistics, censored type-II order statistics, and records based on the parameters and underlying distribution.
conclusion: The framework generalizes known results and applies to a wide range of distribution families.

title: A Min-Max Gradient Search Method For Constrained Simulation Optimization
authors: Ruiyang Jin, Siyang Gao, Henry Lam
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Constrained simulation optimization (CSO) is a general framework for optimizing stochastic systems under performance constraints. It arises widely in practice where objective and constraint evaluations are available only through noisy simulation outputs. Compared with the unconstrained setting, the lack of accessible analytical gradients for simulation-based constraints makes it more challenging to develop efficient solution methods and establish non-asymptotic guarantees. To address this gap, we propose a novel single-loop algorithm, called min-max gradient search (MGS), which integrates a primal-dual framework with stochastic gradient estimators. Unlike conventional stochastic approximation methods based on gradient descent for solving simulation optimization problems, such as Zhou and Bhatnagar (2017) and Hu and Fu (2025), MGS performs alternating gradient descent and ascent on the primal and dual variables, which improves the objective while penalizing constraint violations. For the first time, we establish a finite-time convergence guarantee for single-loop CSO algorithms by showing that MGS converges to a stationary solution (a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker point under mild conditions) at a rate of [MATH], where [MATH] is the number of iterations.
